title: I'm not a programmer. I shipped a cinema management game on Steam with Claude in 60 days
author: Hiroshi_S
selftext:
I'm not a programmer. I designed the game systems and did the playtesting. Claude wrote all of the code, and every image in the game, logo included, came from an image generator. It's called NOW SHOWING and it's out on Steam now.

[Time table, main screen of this game.](https://preview.redd.it/4gt6i88bdosh1.png?width=1920&format=png&auto=webp&s=102d4c26c8de1d622d5b63abef93bc7a456ba898)

Two things helped the most.

Claude doesn't remember between sessions, and my chat Claude and Claude Code can't see each other's conversations. So every decision went into one plain text file, [DESIGN.md](http://DESIGN.md), before anything got built. It ended up at 10,407 lines, with the reason written next to each rule. When Claude or I broke a rule, the mistake went in next to it too.

Image generators are great at one strong picture and bad at hundreds of consistent sprites. So I designed the game around a weekly timetable board and never show the inside of the cinema.

[The game logo generated by AI.](https://preview.redd.it/gmk0d1dfdosh1.png?width=1232&format=png&auto=webp&s=de02b53d8864b31dad693c550a9041c415869882)

How do you keep AI on the same page over a long project?

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5066560/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5066560/)

comments.author: max13007
comments.body:
Firstly, bold of you to charge $13 for something you shipped in 60 days. I'm not sure I'd advise that. 

To answer your question, I do all of my sessions directly in Claude Code. I keep a local git repository which allows Claude to read up on what it needs to know each time I start a new prompt. I have a MD file I have Claude occasionally update with some important details, but largely I leave it to its own devices - will regular cleanup sessions to make sure everything is in good shape, diff reviews, etc... If i do something elsewhere with another model or in chat instead of code, i just have that LLM make a handoff message that contains whatever info i need, and place relevant supporting files into a folder in the Claude Code access tree so it has access to it.

replies.author: Hiroshi_S
replies.body:
Thanks, this is really helpful. Fair point on the price, and "clinical-looking" is honest feedback I needed to hear. For me the fun is in the trade-offs when you rearrange the week, but I clearly haven't shown that well on the store page yet.

The handoff idea is great. I was doing a manual version of it, copying decisions from chat into the file myself. Having the other model write the handoff and dropping it into a folder Claude Code can read is much cleaner. I'll try that.

replies.author: max13007
replies.body: Sure thing - there's likely some people who would pay even more than that for something if it has a lot of depth. Best of luck.

comments.author: bieker
comments.body:
Think about having claude break your [DESIGN.md](http://DESIGN.md) up into multiple files.  In my case my project has a 'documentation' folder with an [index.md](http://index.md), and then a file for each system, subject, style guide, lore etc.  [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) has a pointer to the index and an instruction to offer to update the documentation when new decisions are made about gameplay, systems or style.

Every brainstorming session results in more small md files in the doc directory and the index is updated.  That way when i'm working on a particular backend system the context does not get stuffed with a bunch of unrelated information and Claude can go pick and choose what relevant documentation to read.  The doc folder slowly becomes the GDD, it has character sheets and style guides for each faction and their lore etc as well as technical decisions about specific subsystems.

replies.author: Hiroshi_S
replies.body: This is really useful, thank you. My single file ended up at over 10,000 lines, so an index plus one file per system, with [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) pointing to the index, makes a lot of sense. I can see how that keeps the context much cleaner. I also like the instruction to offer to update the docs when a decision is made, instead of relying on me to remember. I'll set up my next project that way.
